issues.failure_explanation: For functions $f, g \in C(G, \mathbb{T})$ taking values in the circle $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, the convex combination $t f(x) + (1-t) g(x) \pmod 1$ is mathematically ill-defined because scalar multiplication by $t \in [0,1]$ is not well-defined on $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ (choosing representatives in $\mathbb{R}$ differs by an integer $k$, giving $tk \pmod 1$, which depends on $k$). Even if representatives are chosen pointwise (e.g. in $[0,1)$), the resulting map $F(t,x)$ is in general discontinuous across branches whenever winding numbers are non-zero. Furthermore, maps with non-trivial winding numbers cannot be lifted to continuous real-valued functions on $G$, and the displayed calculation in the proof treats values of $f_\gamma$ as real numbers while ignoring the integer jumps across the boundaries of the loops.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula with a valid homotopy: show that since $\bar\omega(f) = \bar\omega(g)$, the difference map $f - g \in C(G, \mathbb{T})$ has degree zero on all loops in $\mathcal{P}$, which allows lifting $f - g$ to a continuous real-valued function $\phi \in C(G, \mathbb{R})$ via the approximating graphs $\Gamma_m$, and then define the homotopy by $F(t,x) = g(x) + t\phi(x) \pmod 1$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 2.3 fails to construct a valid homotopy between continuous circle-valued maps with identical degree vectors.
issues.title: Homotopy between circle-valued maps on SG is ill-defined and discontinuous
issues.why_classification: The classification theorem statement itself is true, but repairing the proof requires establishing a lifting lemma for maps from $G$ to $\mathbb{T}$ with trivial winding numbers, which is a contained nontrivial argument beyond local typo correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 8.2 breaks down in several essential ways: (1) The space $H_m^k$ is defined as a subset of $L(V_m^k, \mathbb{R})$, yet the jump conditions evaluate $f$ at cut points $v_i^{(m)} = \xi(\gamma_i^{(m)}) \in V_{m+1} \setminus V_m$, where functions on $V_m$ are not defined. (2) Minimizing $E[\Gamma_m^k]$ on functions defined on $V_m$ cannot yield a function on $\Gamma_{m+1}^0$. (3) The proof asserts that the result can be harmonically extended 'as in Lemma 5.2' (Theorem 5.2 in the text) to a dense subset of $\tilde{K}$, but Theorem 5.2 provides no extension procedure, only a symmetry-based proof of harmonicity at a single cut point on the Sierpinski Gasket. For general p.c.f. fractals, no valid harmonic extension algorithm on the multi-sheeted covering space with multiple cut points is defined, analyzed, or shown to produce a harmonic map. (4) For general p.c.f. fractals, graph cycles in $\Gamma_m$ are not topological paths in $K$, leaving the degree condition (8.9) undefined.

failure_location.quote:
Repeating the energy minimization along the lines of Lemma \ref{lem.minimizer} results in a unique harmonic 
function on $\Gamma_{m+1}^0$. This can be harmonically extended as in Lemma \ref{lem.ext_harmonic_on_G} to a dense set of $\tilde{K}$, and further extended by uniform continuity to obtain a harmonic function on the entire $\tilde{K}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate a well-defined topological loop space and degree condition for general p.c.f. fractals, correct the level indexing of the discrete spaces and cut points, and provide a rigorous proof that harmonic extension on the covering space converges to a continuous circle-valued map satisfying the Laplace equation across all sheet junctions.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 8.2, which claims the existence of circle-valued harmonic maps for general p.c.f. fractals, is entirely unsupported.
issues.title: Unsound setup and incomplete proof of existence of harmonic maps on p.c.f. fractals
issues.why_classification: The extension of the harmonic map construction from the Sierpinski Gasket to general p.c.f. fractals is one of the paper's principal advertised contributions, but its formal execution lacks the necessary architecture and proof arguments.
